records.subject: Concern over distress faced by tobacco farmers of Andhra Pradesh.
Concern over the difficulties faced by Tobacco Farmers in Andhra Pradesh.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Yerram Venkata Subba Reddy:

Andhra Pradesh accounts for about 22% of India?s total tobacco production, making it one of the largest producing States in the country. Tobacco farmers in districts such as Prakasam, Nellore, and parts of the Godavari region, are facing mounting distress due to declining auction prices, reduced procurement, and the impact of recent tax and regulatory changes affecting the legal tobacco market. Thousands of small and marginal farmers dependent on FCV (Flue-cured Virginia) tobacco cultivation have expressed concern over falling returns, rising input costs, and growing uncertainty about future viability. While public health objectives remain paramount, the livelihoods of lakhs of rural families engaged in tobacco cultivation and allied activities must also be safeguarded. Many farmers have limited access to viable alternative crops due to soil suitability, established credit linkages, and existing market infrastructure. Abrupt market contraction without transition support risks pushing farmers into indebtedness and economic instability. In view of the above, I urge the Government to consider a comprehensive support mechanism, including price stabilization measures, credit restructuring assistance, export facilitation, and a phased crop diversification programme with assured market linkage. A balanced approach is essential to protect rural livelihoods while upholding national public health priorities. ???

(ENDS)

records.subject: Concern over problems being faced by chili farmers in Andhra Pradesh.
records.SM_Text:
Shri Yerram Venkata Subba Reddy: Chilis constitute nearly 40% of India?s total spice exports and Andhra Pradesh is largest Chili producer in India.? Being largest in Asia, Guntur Chili market sets domestic and global Chili price trends.? But this season, price of Chili has fallen to Rs.7,000/quintal when compared to last year?s Rs.28,000/quintal.​ ?????? Chili farmers are demanding remunerative price for Chilis.? Government of India (GOI), after demand by former Andhra Pradesh CM, implementedMarket Intervention Scheme (MIS) by fixing price at Rs.11,781/quintal, with a condition that it will buy only 25% of total stock. ​Hence, I demand:➢ For fixing MSP for Chili at Rs.20,000/quintal.➢ GOI invoke Price Deficiency Payment Scheme and procure 100% Chilis from farmers.➢ GOI should bear entire cost of procurement.➢ Union Cabinet take stock of situation and, if need be, approve above and other proposals in favour of farmers.➢ Restore RBK system, introduce free crop insurance scheme in Andhra Pradesh and strengthen e-Crop.

(ENDS)
